title: Delayed usage bundle shipper for Private deployments (batched, verifiable exports)
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a resilient, auditable exporter that runs inside Private/VPC/on-prem installations to produce periodic usage bundles that can be delivered to Redwood control plane after long network outages or air-gapped windows. The exporter must: 1) produce compact, append-only bundles (gzipped protobuf ledger + signed manifest) with deterministic checkpointing; 2) support incremental checkpoints so installers can ship only deltas; 3) embed cryptographic integrity (Merkle root signatures) and per-tenant counters for reconciliation; 4) allow local rate-limiting/quotas enforcement but still capture raw request telemetry for billing correctness; 5) support multiple delivery mechanisms (SFTP, S3-compatible gateway, removable media manifest) and a clear retry/backoff policy for eventual delivery.
acceptance_criteria: Bundles are generated on configurable cadence (default 1h) and pass integrity verification in control plane
Control plane can reconcile incremental bundles and detect missing sequences with explicit gap reports
Delivery adapter supports S3-compatible endpoints and a 'bundle drop' directory for air-gapped workflows
Local rate limiter counters are logged in the bundle so billing reconciler can distinguish enforcement vs usage
End-to-end e2e test covering 48h offline then catch-up delivery with duplicate-suppression passes in CI
design_notes: Bundle format: sequence-numbered gzipped protobuf ledger + JSON manifest containing start_ts, end_ts, merkle_root, signer_key_id, tenant_id, bundle_size_bytes
Checkpointing: write to local append-only store (wal) with a compact index file to efficiently assemble deltas
Integrity: sign manifest with local KMS/HSM (if configured) or fallback to instance ephemeral key; include public key fingerprint for remote verification
Delivery adapters: implement S3 (minio-compatible), SFTP, and a simple filesystem 'drop' agent for on-prem operators
Quota interplay: exporter records both accepted and rate-limited request counts; reconciler uses these to compute billed units and highlight enforcement anomalies
Backpressure: exporter should not block serving runtime; it must snapshot WAL asynchronously and apply bounded memory/IO constraints

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: operators may deliver bundles out-of-order or resend duplicates; Mitigation: manifest includes monotonic sequence and implement idempotent ingestion with sequence tombstones
Risk: signing keys compromise; Mitigation: allow rotation and include key_id and rotation history in manifest, require security review
Risk: large backlogs stall node IO; Mitigation: chunk bundling and cap memory, provide admin throttle controls
Risk: mismatch between local rate-limiter metrics and control plane view; Mitigation: bundle contains both raw request logs (sampled) and counters to reconcile enforcement differences
